subject.title: Bug: Orphaned TaskFlows in `waiting` status permanently block agent heartbeats (requests-in-flight deadlock)

question: What default abandonment contract, if any, should OpenClaw apply to managed TaskFlows parked in `waiting` before runtime may mark them `lost` and release heartbeat busy state?
rationale: The source confirms stale waits can persist, but the plugin API deliberately exposes durable waits without a timeout and the direct heartbeat busy owner is not yet proven, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent lifecycle contract.

options.title: Define explicit wait ownership
options.body: Add a controller-visible deadline, abandonment signal, or proven orphan predicate before terminalizing existing `waiting` flows, then prove gateway recovery against the reported deadlock.

options.title: Limit recovery to operator repair
options.body: Keep default durable waits intact and expose a safer doctor/tasks maintenance repair path for operators to inspect and expire known orphaned flows manually.

options.title: Pause for live diagnosis
options.body: Hold implementation until a current-main gateway repro identifies whether flow state, pending final delivery, active reply runs, or session lanes are the lasting busy resource.

recommendation.title: Define explicit wait ownership
recommendation.body: Add a controller-visible deadline, abandonment signal, or proven orphan predicate before terminalizing existing `waiting` flows, then prove gateway recovery against the reported deadlock.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest recent history in TaskFlow maintenance and audit code, which is the core lifecycle surface needing a contract decision.
